facts.statement: The genus name Eogavialis was proposed by Eric Buffetaut in 1982 to reassign species previously placed in Tomistoma.
facts.quote: Eric Buffetaut proposed the genus name Eogavialis in 1982 and reassigned both T. africanum and T. gavialoides to it.

facts.statement: The earliest specimens of Eogavialis date back to the Priabonian stage of the late Eocene, between 37.2 and 33.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: dating back to the Priabonian stage of the late Eocene 37.2 to 33.9 million years ago.

facts.statement: Specimens from Kenya date to the late Miocene and early Pliocene, between 11.61 and 2.59 million years ago, extending the known range of the genus.
facts.quote: A third species was assigned to Eogavialis in 2003 from material found in the 1990s from the lower Nawata Formation of the Turkana basin outcropping in Lothagam, Kenya. The strata from which the material was found dates back to the late Miocene and early Pliocene, around 11.61 to 2.59 million years ago.

facts.statement: The fossil record of Eogavialis spans from the Priabonian to the Messinian, covering 37.71 to 5.333 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Priabonian to Messinian (37.71 to 5.333 million years ago)

facts.statement: Eogavialis likely inhabited broad, shallow, meandering rivers in its environment.
facts.quote: A broad, shallow, meandering river is thought to have existed at the time of deposition, suitable for an aquatic gavialid such as Eogavialis.

facts.statement: Some fossils suggest that Eogavialis may have been adapted to coastal marine habitats, unlike most modern crocodilians.
facts.quote: Some specimens of Eogavialis are known from these strata as well, suggesting that the genus may also have been adapted to a coastal marine habitat.

facts.statement: A prominent crista running along the postorbital bone indicates that Eogavialis is a gavialid.
facts.quote: The presence of a prominent crista that runs along the postorbital in Eogavialis testifies to its position as a gavialid.

facts.statement: Some researchers argue that several species previously named under Tomistoma are junior synonyms of Eogavialis africanum because they are morphologically indistinguishable.
facts.quote: In 2000, Brochu and Gingerich argued that T. gavialoides, T. kerunense and T. tenuirostre are all junior synonyms of Eogavialis africanum, since they're morphologically indistinguishable with the only difference in stratigraphic position.
